title: The Triumph of Truth
summary: A man and an evil spirit both claim the same mithun. Matai, the daughter of the Creator, sets a fair test at a bridge, and the truth is revealed without any fighting.
from: Adi folktale, Arunachal Pradesh (retold by Obang Tayeng in Folk Tales of the Adis)
levelReason: The supplied text uses formal, abstract vocabulary (magnificent, astonished, claimants, demonstrated, genuine, restored) and fairly long, complex sentences of about 13 words on average, with a reflective ending about justice and fairness. This is closest to Level 3 (Mighty Tree, grades 8-10).

en: Long ago, in the green hills of Arunachal Pradesh, there lived a man named Da:di Somi. He had a big, strong mithun. People in the hills value the mithun very much.
Da:di Somi took good care of his mithun. It was an important part of his home.
One day, an evil spirit named MédéngSene came. He said, “This mithun is mine!”
Da:di Somi was shocked. He knew the mithun was his. But the spirit would not listen.
They began to quarrel badly. Neither one would give up the mithun. Neither could make the other agree.
Luckily, Matai, the daughter of the Creator, heard about the quarrel.
Matai wanted a fair answer. She did not want anyone to win by scaring or fighting. So she made a simple test.
A bridge would be built. Each of them would lead the mithun across it. The true owner could lead it safely over.
Da:di Somi said yes.
It was his turn first. He walked up to the mithun calmly. The mithun knew him and did what he said. They crossed the bridge safely together.
Everyone watched in wonder.
Then it was MédéngSene’s turn. He took hold of the mithun boldly. He tried to lead it over the same bridge.
Then something surprising happened. The bridge broke and fell down under them.
The test had shown the truth. Da:di Somi and the mithun truly cared for each other. The mithun trusted him and followed him. MédéngSene had told a lie, so he could not do the same.
Matai said that Da:di Somi was the true owner. The mithun went back to him. Justice was done.
The people learned something. We do not need a fight to find the truth. Fairness and wisdom can end an argument.
Moral: Lies cannot take the place of truth and real love. Justice belongs to people who are honest.
hi: बहुत पहले अरुणाचल प्रदेश की हरी-भरी पहाड़ियों में दा:दी सोमी नाम का एक आदमी रहता था। उसके पास मिथुन नाम का एक बड़ा और ताकतवर जानवर था। पहाड़ों के लोग मिथुन को बहुत कीमती मानते हैं।
दा:दी सोमी अपने मिथुन की अच्छी देखभाल करता था। वह उसके घर का ज़रूरी हिस्सा था।
एक दिन मेदेंगसेने नाम की एक बुरी आत्मा आई। उसने कहा, “यह मिथुन मेरा है!”
दा:दी सोमी हैरान रह गया। वह जानता था कि मिथुन उसका है। पर आत्मा सुनने को तैयार नहीं थी।
दोनों में बुरी तरह झगड़ा होने लगा। कोई भी मिथुन को छोड़ने को तैयार नहीं था। कोई दूसरे को मना भी नहीं पा रहा था।
अच्छी बात यह हुई कि सृष्टिकर्ता की बेटी माताई ने इस झगड़े के बारे में सुन लिया।
माताई चाहती थी कि फ़ैसला न्याय से हो। वह नहीं चाहती थी कि कोई डराकर या लड़कर जीते। इसलिए उसने एक आसान परीक्षा सोची।
एक पुल बनाया जाएगा। दोनों बारी-बारी से मिथुन को उस पर से ले जाएँगे। जो असली मालिक होगा, वही उसे सुरक्षित पार करा पाएगा।
दा:दी सोमी ने हाँ कह दी।
पहले उसकी बारी आई। वह शांति से मिथुन के पास गया। मिथुन ने उसे पहचान लिया और उसकी बात मानी। दोनों साथ-साथ पुल पार कर गए।
सब लोग हैरानी से देखते रह गए।
फिर मेदेंगसेने की बारी आई। उसने बड़े भरोसे से मिथुन को पकड़ा। वह उसी पुल से उसे ले जाने लगा।
तभी कुछ अनोखा हुआ। पुल टूट गया और उनके नीचे गिर पड़ा।
परीक्षा ने सच दिखा दिया। दा:दी सोमी और मिथुन के बीच सचमुच प्यार का रिश्ता था। मिथुन उस पर भरोसा करता था और उसके पीछे चला। मेदेंगसेने ने झूठ बोला था, इसलिए वह ऐसा नहीं कर सका।
माताई ने कहा कि दा:दी सोमी ही असली मालिक है। मिथुन उसे लौटा दिया गया। न्याय हुआ।
लोगों ने सीखा कि सच जानने के लिए लड़ाई की ज़रूरत नहीं होती। निष्पक्षता और समझदारी से झगड़ा सुलझाया जा सकता है।
सीख: झूठ सच की और सच्चे रिश्ते की जगह नहीं ले सकता। न्याय उन्हीं का होता है जो ईमानदार रहते हैं।

questions.q: Who owned the mithun, and who said it was his?
What was the test that Matai planned?
What happened to the bridge when MédéngSene tried to lead the mithun?
How do you think Da:di Somi felt when the spirit said the mithun was his?
Why is it good to tell the truth, even when it is hard?

en: Long ago, in the beautiful hills of Arunachal Pradesh, there lived a man named Da:di Somi. He owned a fine, strong mithun, an animal that the people of the region valued greatly.
Da:di Somi looked after his mithun carefully and thought of it as an important part of his household.
One day, an evil spirit named MédéngSene appeared and said that the mithun belonged to him.
Da:di Somi was surprised and upset. He knew the mithun was his, but the spirit would not listen to him.
Their argument grew into a serious dispute. Neither of them would give up the animal, and neither could convince the other.
Luckily, Matai, the daughter of the Creator, heard about their quarrel.
She wanted the matter settled fairly, so that nobody could win by using threats or force. Instead, she suggested a simple test.
A bridge would be built, and each of them would be asked to lead the mithun across it. The true owner would be able to guide the animal safely over.
Da:di Somi agreed.
When it was his turn, he walked up to the mithun calmly. The animal knew him and obeyed him, and together they crossed the bridge safely.
Everyone watched in amazement.
Then it was MédéngSene’s turn. The spirit took hold of the mithun confidently and tried to lead it across the same bridge.
But then something unexpected happened. As MédéngSene tried to guide the animal, the bridge collapsed beneath them.
The test had shown the truth. Da:di Somi had proved his real bond with the mithun, which trusted him and followed him willingly. MédéngSene, who had made a false claim, could not do the same.
Matai declared that Da:di Somi was the rightful owner. The mithun was given back to him, and justice was done.
The people understood that the truth can be found without violence when fairness and wisdom guide the solving of a dispute.
Moral: False claims cannot replace the truth or a real bond. In the end, justice belongs to people who act honestly.
hi: बहुत समय पहले अरुणाचल प्रदेश की सुंदर पहाड़ियों में दा:दी सोमी नाम का एक आदमी रहता था। उसके पास एक शानदार मिथुन था, जिसे वहाँ के लोग बहुत कीमती मानते थे।
दा:दी सोमी अपने मिथुन की बड़े ध्यान से देखभाल करता था और उसे अपने घर-परिवार का ज़रूरी हिस्सा समझता था।
एक दिन मेदेंगसेने नाम की एक दुष्ट आत्मा आई और बोली कि यह मिथुन उसका है।
दा:दी सोमी हैरान और परेशान हो गया। वह जानता था कि मिथुन उसी का है, लेकिन आत्मा उसकी बात सुनने को तैयार नहीं थी।
उनकी बहस बढ़कर गंभीर विवाद बन गई। कोई भी मिथुन को छोड़ने को राज़ी नहीं था, और कोई दूसरे को समझा नहीं पा रहा था।
सौभाग्य से सृष्टिकर्ता की बेटी माताई को उनके झगड़े का पता चल गया।
वह चाहती थी कि मामला निष्पक्ष ढंग से सुलझे, ताकि कोई धमकी या ज़ोर-ज़बरदस्ती से न जीते। इसलिए उसने एक सीधी-सी परीक्षा सुझाई।
एक पुल बनाया जाएगा और दोनों से कहा जाएगा कि वे बारी-बारी से मिथुन को उसके पार ले जाएँ। जो सचमुच मालिक होगा, वही जानवर को सुरक्षित पार करा सकेगा।
दा:दी सोमी मान गया।
जब उसकी बारी आई, तो वह शांति से मिथुन के पास गया। मिथुन ने उसे पहचाना और उसका कहा माना, और दोनों साथ मिलकर सुरक्षित पुल पार कर गए।
सब लोग हैरत से देखते रहे।
फिर मेदेंगसेने की बारी आई। आत्मा ने पूरे भरोसे के साथ मिथुन को पकड़ा और उसी पुल से ले जाने की कोशिश की।
लेकिन तभी कुछ अनहोनी हो गई। जैसे ही मेदेंगसेने मिथुन को आगे बढ़ाने लगा, पुल उनके नीचे टूटकर गिर गया।
परीक्षा ने सच सामने ला दिया। दा:दी सोमी ने मिथुन के साथ अपना सच्चा रिश्ता साबित कर दिया था; मिथुन उस पर भरोसा करता था और खुशी से उसके पीछे चला। झूठा दावा करने वाला मेदेंगसेने ऐसा नहीं कर पाया।
माताई ने घोषणा की कि दा:दी सोमी ही असली मालिक है। मिथुन उसे लौटा दिया गया और न्याय हुआ।
लोगों ने समझा कि जब निष्पक्षता और समझदारी झगड़े को सुलझाने में रास्ता दिखाती हैं, तो सच बिना हिंसा के भी सामने आ सकता है।
सीख: झूठे दावे सच और सच्चे रिश्ते की जगह नहीं ले सकते। न्याय आख़िरकार उन्हीं का होता है जो ईमानदारी से काम करते हैं।

questions.q: Why did Matai choose a test instead of letting Da:di Somi and MédéngSene settle it by force?
Why do you think the mithun followed Da:di Somi but not MédéngSene?
Why did Da:di Somi agree to the test straight away? What does that tell you about him?
What might have happened if Matai had not heard about the quarrel?
The bridge collapsed under MédéngSene. What do you think the story is trying to show us by this?

en: Long ago, in the beautiful hills of Arunachal Pradesh, there lived a man named Da:di Somi. He owned a magnificent mithun, a powerful animal highly valued by the people of the region.
Da:di Somi cared for his mithun and considered it an important part of his household.
One day, an evil spirit named MédéngSene appeared and claimed that the animal belonged to him.
Da:di Somi was astonished. He knew that the mithun was his, but the spirit refused to listen.
The disagreement grew into a serious dispute. Neither would surrender the animal, and neither could convince the other.
Fortunately, Matai, the daughter of the Creator, learned about their quarrel.
She decided that the dispute should be settled fairly. Rather than allowing either of them to win through threats or force, she proposed a simple test.
A bridge would be built, and both claimants would be asked to lead the mithun across it. Whoever truly owned the animal would be able to guide it safely over the bridge.
Da:di Somi agreed.
When his turn came, he approached the mithun calmly. The animal recognised him and followed his instructions. Together, they walked across the bridge safely.
Everyone watched in amazement.
Then it was MédéngSene’s turn. The spirit confidently took hold of the mithun and attempted to lead it across the same bridge.
But something unexpected happened. As MédéngSene tried to guide the animal, the bridge collapsed beneath them.

The test had revealed the truth. Da:di Somi had demonstrated his genuine bond with the mithun. The animal trusted him and willingly followed him across the bridge. MédéngSene, who had falsely claimed ownership, could not achieve the same result.
Matai declared Da:di Somi the rightful owner. The mithun was returned to him, and justice was restored.
The people understood that the truth could be established without violence when fairness and wisdom guided the resolution of a dispute.
Moral: Truth and genuine relationships cannot be replaced by false claims. Justice ultimately belongs to those who act honestly.
hi: बहुत पहले, अरुणाचल प्रदेश की सुंदर पहाड़ियों में दा:दी सोमी नाम का एक व्यक्ति रहता था। उसके पास एक भव्य मिथुन था, एक शक्तिशाली पशु, जिसे इस क्षेत्र के लोग बहुत मूल्यवान मानते थे।
दा:दी सोमी अपने मिथुन की स्नेह से देखभाल करता था और उसे अपने घर-परिवार का एक महत्वपूर्ण हिस्सा मानता था।
एक दिन मेदेंगसेने नाम की एक दुष्ट आत्मा प्रकट हुई और उसने दावा किया कि वह पशु उसका है।
दा:दी सोमी स्तब्ध रह गया। वह जानता था कि मिथुन उसी का है, पर आत्मा कुछ सुनने को तैयार नहीं थी।
असहमति बढ़ते-बढ़ते गंभीर विवाद बन गई। न कोई पशु को छोड़ने को तैयार था, न कोई दूसरे को कायल कर पा रहा था।
सौभाग्य से सृष्टिकर्ता की पुत्री माताई को उनके इस झगड़े की ख़बर मिल गई।
उसने तय किया कि विवाद का निपटारा न्यायपूर्ण ढंग से होना चाहिए। किसी को धमकी या बल से जीतने देने के बजाय उसने एक सरल परीक्षा प्रस्तावित की।
एक पुल बनाया जाएगा और दोनों दावेदारों से कहा जाएगा कि वे मिथुन को उसके पार ले जाएँ। जो सचमुच उसका स्वामी होगा, वही उसे सुरक्षित रूप से पुल पार करा पाएगा।
दा:दी सोमी ने सहमति दे दी।
जब उसकी बारी आई, तो वह शांत भाव से मिथुन के पास पहुँचा। पशु ने उसे पहचाना और उसके निर्देशों का पालन किया। दोनों साथ-साथ सकुशल पुल के पार चले गए।
सब लोग विस्मय से देखते रह गए।
फिर मेदेंगसेने की बारी आई। आत्मा ने पूरे आत्मविश्वास से मिथुन को थामा और उसी पुल से उसे पार ले जाने का प्रयास किया।
पर तभी कुछ अप्रत्याशित घटा। मेदेंगसेने ने जैसे ही पशु को आगे बढ़ाना चाहा, पुल उनके नीचे ढह गया।
परीक्षा ने सच उजागर कर दिया था। दा:दी सोमी ने मिथुन के साथ अपने सच्चे लगाव को सिद्ध कर दिया था; पशु उसका विश्वास करता था और स्वेच्छा से उसके पीछे चला। झूठा दावा करने वाला मेदेंगसेने वही नहीं कर सका।
माताई ने दा:दी सोमी को सही स्वामी घोषित किया। मिथुन उसे लौटा दिया गया और न्याय की पुनर्स्थापना हुई।
लोगों ने समझा कि जब निष्पक्षता और विवेक किसी विवाद के समाधान का मार्ग दिखाते हैं, तब सत्य बिना हिंसा के भी स्थापित हो सकता है।
सीख: सत्य और सच्चे संबंधों की जगह झूठे दावे नहीं ले सकते। न्याय अंततः उन्हीं का होता है जो ईमानदारी से आचरण करते हैं।

questions.q: Is a test like Matai’s a fair way to settle a dispute? What would make any way of settling a dispute fair to both sides?
How might MédéngSene have explained his claim? Why might a person or being make a claim they know is false?
The story says the mithun is highly valued by the people of the region. What does the story suggest about the bond between a person and an animal they care for?
The moral says that truth and genuine relationships cannot be replaced by false claims. What does a genuine relationship look like, and why can it not be faked?
Today, how do people try to settle disputes without threats or force? Think of examples such as talking it through, elders, mediators or courts, and ask what each needs in order to be fair.

scenes.p: Wide storybook illustration of green, misty hills in Arunachal Pradesh at morning. Da:di Somi, a calm middle-aged man in simple handwoven clothes with a kind face, gently strokes his mithun, a large dark-bodied bovine with white lower legs and broad curved horns, outside his home. Warm, peaceful mood, soft natural colours.

scenes.th: आत्मा मिथुन पर दावा करती है
scenes.p: Da:di Somi stands protectively beside his mithun, astonished and worried, while MédéngSene, a tall shadowy spirit made of dark drifting mist with glowing pale eyes (mysterious, not gory), points at the mithun as if claiming it. Tense, dusky hill-side setting; the mithun looks uneasy.

scenes.th: माताई एक न्यायपूर्ण परीक्षा सोचती है
scenes.p: Matai, the daughter of the Creator, a dignified young woman surrounded by a soft golden glow, stands between Da:di Somi and MédéngSene, one hand raised calmly, pointing toward a gorge where villagers are beginning to build a simple bridge. Hopeful, fair-minded mood.

scenes.th: दा:दी सोमी पुल पार करता है
scenes.p: Da:di Somi walks calmly across a simple bridge over a deep green gorge with the mithun following willingly right behind him, its head relaxed. Villagers watch from the bank with wide eyes. Bright, wondering mood.

MédéngSene grips the mithun's rope and pulls it onto the same bridge; the planks and ropes are splitting and the bridge is breaking apart, with the spirit tumbling in a swirl of dark mist (no injury shown) and the mithun safely stepping back toward the bank. Dramatic but child-friendly.

Matai stands in golden light and gestures toward Da:di Somi, who reunites with his mithun, resting his hand on its neck while it leans into him. The villagers gather around nodding. Warm, relieved, joyful mood.

Quiet evening scene: villagers sit in a circle with Da:di Somi and his mithun resting in the foreground, talking peacefully. In the background, the repaired path over the gorge glows in sunset light. Calm, thoughtful, hopeful mood.

about.where: Arunachal Pradesh is a state in the hills of far north-eastern India. This version is described as an Adi folktale. The Adi are one of the many indigenous communities of the state, and research on Adi society has been carried out in places such as East Siang district.
about.community: The repository names this as an Adi folktale retold by Obang Tayeng in Folk Tales of the Adis (Mittal Publications, 2003). Arunachal Pradesh has many different communities and languages, so this one story cannot speak for all of them, or even for every Adi person.
about.tradition: Adi folk tales are told as part of a living oral storytelling tradition. This version is a written retelling in a book, so the words you read are the retelling author’s and the project team’s, not an exact record of how any storyteller told it aloud.
about.shared: In the story, the mithun is a powerful animal highly valued by the people of the region. A study of Adi society describes the mithun as a store of wealth that is also important in rituals, and in settling disputes and compensation. This helps explain why a quarrel over one mithun could matter so much.
about.matters: This is one version from one source, not the only one. The story shows that fairness and wisdom can settle a dispute without threats or force, and that a true bond cannot be faked. Matai’s role in the story is to make sure the test is fair to both sides.
